headline: Trump says US aid to Israel ends this year, America votes amid scanner trouble, and Binance explains its $6.3bn hack

stories.title: Trump says the US will stop paying Israel's $4bn a year in military aid at the end of this year
facts: In a Fox News phone interview on Election Day morning, Trump said he and Netanyahu agreed "months ago" that the $4bn a year would stop: "by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel."
He added that the US would still "help Israel if they need it" and that Israel can buy US weapons.
It's unclear which funds he means: the current memorandum of understanding gives Israel $3.8bn a year in military aid and runs until the end of 2028, the BBC notes.
Trump accused Democrats of using aid to Israel as a "talking point" against Republicans; the White House and Netanyahu's office hadn't clarified or commented at the time of reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: US military aid has underpinned Israel's defence planning for decades, so an early end would be a major policy shift, if the White House confirms it.

stories.title: America votes: ballot scanners fail in a key New York swing district, and the DOJ sends monitors to all 50 states
facts: Nearly 60 million people had already voted early, about half of the roughly 122 million who voted in the 2022 midterms, per the University of Florida's Election Lab.

Ballot scanners across Westchester County rejected ballots because the paper was too thick; voters are putting ballots in orange emergency bags to be counted later. The county is the battleground in NY-17, Lawler vs. Conley.

The Justice Department says it's running its largest monitoring effort ever, about 1,000 monitors in all 50 states for the first time, though an official told a court on Monday the number was closer to 900.
CNN notes gas has never been as expensive on an Election Day as it is today.
Polls in New York close at 9pm ET, which is 3am Berlin time, so the first big results land overnight.
stories.whyItMatters: Control of Congress for Trump's last two years is on the line, and early glitches like Westchester's tend to fuel fights over the count.

image.alt: Voters wait in line at a polling place in Warrington, Pennsylvania, on Election Day

stories.title: Binance's $6.3bn hack started with a fake developer tool and a fake job interview, and Vercel ships a defence against exactly that
facts: In June, a Binance wallet DevOps engineer installed a tampered Homebrew package for a popular AI coding tool found via a search engine; Binance replaced the device, but the team was already exposed.

In September, attackers posing as recruiters ran video interviews with another engineer; the "coding assignment" downloaded onto his work laptop contained zero-day malware that evaded endpoint security.
On October 20 they used that machine and an internal AI tool to reach two wallet engineers' computers, and on October 29 they abused Ethereum's EIP-7702 to gain execution rights over a hot wallet.
Binance says about 98% of the $6.34bn has been replenished with company funds and $2.85bn is frozen; the FBI links it to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, which Pyongyang denies.

Vercel started rolling out Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) for vercel.com today: session renewal needs a key bound to the device, so cookies stolen by infostealer malware can't practically be reused. Guillermo Rauch pitched it as protection against a "Binance-style attack".
stories.whyItMatters: Fake job interviews and poisoned dev tools are now the front door for the biggest heists, so developer laptops are the real perimeter.

image.alt: CNBC image accompanying the Binance hack report

stories.title: Google: schools that switch off AI completely will lose Google Search too
facts: Google will turn off its AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school admins explicitly enable them, across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom and Search.
But because AI features are now built into Search, schools that restrict AI altogether will lose Search access; students will see a message from their school instead.
Google's education VP Chris Phillips told the New York Times that "Search and AI are deeply integrated." More details for schools come in the coming months.
stories.whyItMatters: With Chromebooks and Google apps everywhere in classrooms, schools effectively have to accept AI Overviews to keep a basic research tool.

facts.text: German pensions are expected to rise by about 4.1% on July 1, 2027, per the labour ministry; exact figures come in March. Pensions rose 4.24% this July.
Melania Trump will bring Russian and Ukrainian representatives to the White House on Thursday, after announcing a ceasefire in the city of Oleshky last month.
Greenland's parliament passed a security agreement with the US that lets Washington expand its military presence, while the island is meant to stay independent.
Anthropic's amended S-1 shows compute ate 58% of revenue last quarter, up from 48%, even as revenue rose to about $17bn from $11.5bn.
More than 1,000 officers raided an alleged "crime as a service" network in the Rhein-Main area accused of money laundering, drug smuggling and covering up undeclared work; five arrests.
GTA VI pre-load starts November 10 ahead of the November 19 launch, with a download of up to 212GB.
Bethesda confirmed the next Elder Scrolls is The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, named after a city in Hammerfell; no release year yet.
Nvidia is the world's most valuable company again as Apple shares slide.

stories.title: Dev notes

facts.text: Claude can now auto-connect plugins at login when their MCP servers accept Claude as a trusted issuer, so users don't have to re-authorize.
Claude Code's October recap: mods, a desktop app that's better at running many sessions side by side, and more insight into where usage goes.
A severe Postman bug report says the desktop app auto-installs Codex and Claude plugins and its installer tries to trust its own startup hook.
Matthew Honnibal argues this morning's "Astra reads and writes weights" post is misleading: the headline Qwen fix used Python and ran the model, and raw-weight reading only covered tiny networks.
Playwright says don't delete it over browser CVEs: no Playwright package bundles a browser, and you should keep browsers updated.
GitHub Copilot is now one of the agents in JetBrains Air, locally or in sandboxed cloud runs with Air Teams.
Google's Project Suncatcher booted data-center TPUs on a prototype satellite and ran Gemma 4 in low Earth orbit.
Microsoft says Windows 11 is now 20% more responsive and 40% faster at multitasking on 8GB PCs.
libghostty IO throughput is up significantly since Ghostty 1.4; most of it gets backported to 1.4.1.
Ubuntu 26.04's Rust sudo isn't fully compatible with standard sudo, and "Death comes for XSLT" tops Lobsters.
Bun merged a PR removing 126 unsafe blocks from its core crates, resolver and package manager.
